content: When the immune system becomes overactive, it may lead to symptoms that can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. While taking this medication, changes in body fat distribution may occur, such as increased fat in the upper back and abdominal areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The exact cause and long-term effects of these changes remain unknown. Efavirenz commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. In adults, this rash may appear within the first two weeks of treatment and typically resolves within four weeks if it is not severe. In children, a rash may develop within the first four weeks of treatment. However, it may be difficult to distinguish a common rash from a rare, severe allergic reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, also contact your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking efavirenz, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Efavirenz may lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood may also heighten this risk, especially if you are using diuretics (water pills) or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Rashes may be more common and severe in children taking efavirenz. Report any rash immediately. Your doctor may prescribe an antihistamine for your child before starting efavirenz to reduce the risk of a rash. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and efavirenz may be part of this treatment. However, this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of efavirenz from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Similarly, efavirenz can accelerate the removal of many other medications, which may impact their efficacy. Certain HIV medications, such as elvitegravir or other NNRTIs (e.g., etravirine, nevirapine, rilpivirine), may interact with efavirenz. If you are taking atazanavir with this medication, you may also need to take ritonavir. Efavirenz may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while on this medication. Check the labels of all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Efavirenz may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine cannabinoid tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests: Regular medical and laboratory tests (e.g., liver function tests, viral load, T-cell counts, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels) should be conducted before starting this medication and during its use. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
